sources_read: .qc-cache/hireops-2026-10-01-transaction-hardening-r2/rules/WebDev Rubrics QC.xlsx: Quality Checks row 32 (check 31), Internal Quality Checks row 32, and full Quality/Deterministic inventory
evidence: Row-specific source Pass: the workbook's public and internal check 31 require collection-wide quantifiers and scoped unchanged guards. Paths below use T=.qc-cache/hireops-2026-10-01-transaction-hardening-r2/task. T/tests/scored/functional/prompt.md:19 requires before/after facts per row and per record, permits generic access/security logs and ordinary extra audit entries, and forbids exact global log counts. Lines 23 and 37 require all three referrers and all nine tier/band pairs; lines 45 and 63 require the complete observed read-family inventory and every non-Finance account's prepare/commit refusals, including cached commits. Corresponding criterion hro_referrer_roster at judge.toml:515 explicitly says every supplied employee and each selection; hro_anon_read_status at :785 requires each observed family. hro_change_readers at :1199 requires every supplied signed-in role. B1 at prompt.md:55 inspects both successors, movements, payments, grants, referrals, member text/snapshots and receipt; judge.toml:956 requires each selected source and exactly one successor, :1109 requires all identities/headrooms, :1118 every member audit line, and :1127 each member snapshot with complete transaction balances. Exactly-one concurrency checks inspect both responses and persisted effect collections, not just one winner (prompt.md:39,47,61; judge.toml:659,704,713,722). P10 at prompt.md:49 and judge.toml:929 compares all recorded records and imported seed identities. The DRAFT probe samples one imported identity, but the supplied seed has exactly one DRAFT (OFF-301), and instruction.md:11 permits omitting operational history; no omitted required DRAFT collection was found. Unchanged guards are bounded appropriately: judge.toml:947 preserves immediately-before-attempt economic/history state while allowing a draft/access logs; :1010 allows the saved preview and generic access logs to grow; :1046 compares both members immediately before a stale commit, preserving the intervening legitimate revision. This matches hireops_rules.md:437-472. The source implements complete member/requisition loops and creates receipts after all member postings (solution/app/src/change-sets.js:49-63,100-136). Raw evidence: all 292 artifact hashes in the inspected index matched. batch-domain.cjs SHA256 80eb13e01fc5d9bb9514bec35721a8c0619dd1eda75c6ed6a48be8c5858a2f0d contains per-member assertions at lines 44,48-54, full financial comparisons at 41,86,92, and all six forbidden actors at 108. Its results.json SHA256 a44c0bf81b27981d9bf1d63239f8b7ce7da5733d6d70aef425e2350a76b7732f reports those finite local observations passed; all four embedded application-source hashes match the frozen task. These are bounded HTTP observations, not a configured judge run, workload measurement, Oracle/model score, or private deterministic suite execution. Full configured evidence remains absent as the index states; this finding establishes only row 31's authored collection/side-effect contract, not overall clearance.
counterexample: Attempted weak alternative: a two-member commit correctly updates the first member but omits the second member's grant/audit snapshot, or posts a partial first-member revision before refusing a stale second source. It cannot satisfy the written row-31 bar: prompt B1 and hro_change_grants/audit/afterimages require both members, while hro_change_stale_leaf checks all members including the still-valid first member. An app that protects only the first observed endpoint also fails the complete-family inventory. Attempted conforming alternative: a refused commit retains its durable draft, appends a generic access log, and preserves another person's intervening revision; a successful commit emits an extra harmless audit line. Those legitimate changes are expressly allowed, and refusal comparison is against immediately-before-attempt state, so no false failure is warranted. No surviving collection-sampling or legitimate-side-effect counterexample was identified.
